speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to Dr. Agent's clinic. I see you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; let's start by asking: How long have you had these symptoms, and do you recall any specific trauma or insect bite?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. speaker: Doctor
text: The timeline of knee pain followed by wrist pain, combined with your recent camping trip in Minnesota, is highly suggestive of a specific tick-borne illness. Have you noticed any rash, particularly between your fingers or on your palms/soles, and do you have a history of tick bites? REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide images of the skin lesions for assessment.

text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

text: The description of painless, violaceous, vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, combined with your recent camping trip in Minnesota and a history of knee pain, is highly specific.
